newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish 1-yr bond seen attractive at 95.00.
newsitem.headline: Polish 1-yr bond seen attractive at 95.00.

text.p: Polish one-year index-linked bonds are seen attractive if the last minimum price of 95.00 holds at Tuesday's 150 million zloty primary tender, analysts said on Monday.
They said investors' bids should total between 70 and 100 million zlotys at the Tuesday tender, up from 69 million at the last one-year bond auction on October 29.
The base interest rate of the bond is the cumulative inflation rate for the 12 months from October 1996 to September 1997, without a premium.

"If the inflation rate between October 1996 and September 1997 is somewhere between 14 and 16 percent, than it would be worth buying at 95.00, with the prospective yield above 20 percent," said Grzegorz Raupuk from Bank Gdanski SA.

Poland cut the minimum price of one-year index-linked bonds to 95.00 from 96.65 at the last auction on October 29. It cut the average price to 95.99, down from 96.75, but sold only six million zlotys worth of the bonds.
The value date for this auction is December 2, 1996 and the bonds mature on December 3, 1997.
